pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes the 11 findings from a wholesale security review, which rated the repository HIGH risk. Both HIGH findings were in `.github/workflows/privacy-review.yml`.

| # | Severity | Finding | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HIGH | A symlink committed in a PR redirected the case-text write onto `.havel/AUDIT.md`, replacing the system prompt | `cc787ff` |
| 2 | HIGH | The documented `python ci/call_model.py` ran the copy the PR edits | `cc787ff` |
| 3 | MEDIUM | The documented `MODEL_API_KEY` secret was undeclared and never mapped into a step | `cc787ff` |
| 4 | MEDIUM | A PR description could plant a competing `DECLARED_SCOPE:` line | `cfdef75` |
| 5 | MEDIUM | The verdict parser passed an echoed format line and glob tokens as APPROVE | `5b7d287` |
| 6 | MEDIUM | Live eval graded only the verdict token, never classes or regimes | `8d79e7c` |
| 7 | MEDIUM | Gate tests read the YAML text and never ran the gate | `5b7d287` |
| 8 | LOW | Repository `.git/config` could make an admitted `git status` run any program | `267aba5` |
| 9 | LOW | A hook test inherited host `GIT_CONFIG_*` vectors and failed in some environments | `4b67596` |
| 10 | LOW | Fork PRs failed the job on `createComment` after an APPROVE | `cc787ff` |
| 11 | LOW | The hook allowlist named missing scripts and denied every command CONTRIBUTING.md requires | `31bcb68` |

## Why one PR spanning 33 files

Twenty of the 33 changed files are generated or fixture data: 16 rebuilt bundles, three new eval fixture files, and the re-hashed manifest. Six more are test modules. The hand-written change is split into nine commits, one finding group each, so the PR can be reviewed commit by commit. All the work lives on a single assigned branch.

## Changes worth reviewing closely

- **Adopter-visible: the model command runs from `base/`.** That directory is a checkout of the calling repository at the PR's base commit. Previously the command ran in the PR tree. A command reading PR files from its working directory was reading the attack surface. This is recorded under `Security` in the CHANGELOG.
- **The case text now carries an `UNTRUSTED CONTENT` frame.** A fresh nonce closes it. `AUDIT.md` step 0b grants scope authority to the opening `DECLARED_SCOPE:` line alone. `eval/run_eval.py` emits the same frame. `context.md` now sits inside the frame after the scope line; previously it preceded the scope line, unlike CI.
- **Local fork of upstream-pinned files.** `hooks/enforce_branch_name.py` and `tests/test_enforce_branch_name.py` now differ from the pinned `abuzucom/agents` commit. `upstream-files.json` was re-hashed through a new `--write-manifest` refresh form, and `docs/template-drift.md` records the fork. The fixes should be ported upstream.
- **`git config` without `--edit` is exempt from the new exec-key gate.** Without the exemption, a flagged key could not be removed, because the gate also blocks file writes to `.git/config`.

## Test-first evidence

Every executable change shipped with tests that were run and seen failing before the fix:
- The `Build case text` behavioral test overwrote a trusted sentinel with case text, reproducing finding 1.
- `ParseVerdictBehaviorTest` passed the template echo and three glob tokens as APPROVE.
- `ExecutableConfigTest` allowed `git status` with `core.fsmonitor` set.
- The new framing and grading tests failed until implemented.

No existing assertion was weakened. No eval case was edited, and one was added (104 total).

## Verification

- CI `checks` passes on `6f95e3e`.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 358 tests pass locally.
- `python eval/run_eval.py`: the structure check validates 104 cases.
- `scripts/build_bundle.py --check`, `scripts/check_regime_refs.py` and `scripts/check_upstream_drift.py --check-local` (26/26) are all clean.
- All five prose checkers over the CI file list. The blocking checkers are clean. The remaining warnings are warning-only, on lines this branch does not touch.

## Outstanding before marking ready

- [ ] **Live corpus run.** AGENTS.md requires one for the `AUDIT.md` step 0b change before it counts as finished. Run `python eval/run_eval.py --model-call <module:fn>` with a real model credential. This session has none. The new grading in `8d79e7c` may surface existing cases where the model's classes or regimes miss the expectation.
- [ ] **Action pins.** Confirm that `actions/checkout@11d5960…` matches `v4.4.0` and `actions/github-script@f28e40c…` matches `v7.1.0`. Neither could be resolved from this session.

pulls.title: fix: address wholesale security review findings

pulls.body:
Follow-up to #1. Two defects in the same family, plus two test defects found along the way.

## 1. The gate accepted a verdict line from any mode

`privacy-review.yml` builds its case text from a pull request diff, so it always runs PR mode. Section 6 gives PR mode one token, `VERDICT`. The `Parse verdict` step grepped:

```
'^(VERDICT|RISK(\s\(partial\))?|ACCURACY):'
```

A report answering in File, Wholesale, Piece, or Data-map mode therefore satisfied the gate. `RISK: NONE-FOUND` reads as a pass under a substring check for `BLOCK`, even though no PR-mode verdict was ever issued and the review made no merge claim. Section 6 is explicit that File and Wholesale carry "No merge claim".

`eval/run_eval.py` graded the same way, so the corpus could not catch it either.

The workflow now greps `'^VERDICT:'` alone. A response in another mode falls through the existing empty-line branch, whose message names PR mode as the reason. `run_eval.py` gains `MODE_VERDICT_TOKENS`:

| Mode | Token |
|---|---|
| PR | `VERDICT` |
| File | `RISK` |
| Wholesale | `RISK` |
| Piece | `RISK (partial)` |
| Data-map | `ACCURACY` |

`verdict_matches` takes a keyword-only `mode` and rejects a mismatched token. The call site passes `case["mode"]`. Keyword-only and added last, so `verdict_matches("BLOCK", text)` keeps working, which matters because adorno calls it positionally in four places.

## 2. The gate read the whole verdict line, not the token

Found in review after the first fix landed. `grep -qE 'BLOCK|NEEDS-HUMAN'` searched the entire line, so the reason decided the outcome:

- **Fails closed** on `VERDICT: APPROVE - resolved earlier BLOCK findings`, failing CI on a valid approve.
- **Fails open** on `VERDICT: REJECT`, which matches neither alternative, sets `blocked=false`, and merges.

The fail-open case is the serious one, and it was pre-existing: the original `grep -q 'BLOCK'` had the same shape.

The gate now takes the token off the front with parameter expansion and branches on it. `APPROVE` passes. `BLOCK` and `NEEDS-HUMAN` honor `fail_on_block`. Anything else exits 1, exactly as a missing `VERDICT:` line already does, because a malformed verdict is not a verdict.

`fail_on_block` keeps its documented meaning. Blocking every non-APPROVE token regardless of that input would break an adopter running advisory-only reviews; a malformed verdict failing the parse step is a different thing from a verdict blocking, and only the latter is what that input governs.

## 3. Two tests that passed for the wrong reason

Both were mine, and both would have survived a revert of the code they cover.

`test_review_greps_the_accuracy_token` asserted `ACCURACY` appears in the workflow. True while the gate grepped every mode's token; after fix 1 the only occurrence is the comment explaining the change. Its name also contradicted `VerdictGateTest`, which asserts the grep line excludes `ACCURACY`. That contract is already covered there precisely, so only the sibling guard survives, renamed: `CONFORMANCE` is adorno's token and must not appear here.

`test_gate_blocks_on_needs_human` asserted over the whole step, and the comment above the gate names `NEEDS-HUMAN`. Reverting to `grep -q 'BLOCK'` left it green. It now reads the step's executable lines.

## 4. The comparison itself was a substring test

`expected_verdict in actual_line` meant an expected `BLOCK` matched `VERDICT: APPROVE - no BLOCK conditions observed`, scoring a failing case as a pass.

The fix splits the reason off at `' - '` and compares against the verdict alone. Getting this right took two attempts, and the second attempt is the interesting one. Fixtures store the verdict in **four** shapes:

| Shape | Example | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Bare severity | `BLOCK` | PR cases |
| Prefixed | `RISK: MEDIUM` | many File cases |
| Prefix alone | `RISK (partial)` | Piece cases |
| Prefix with colon | `RISK:` | **45 File cases here** |

A first pass accepting only the first three broke all 45 of those at once. They use `RISK:` to assert "this mode answered, any severity", and only a substring test had ever accepted it.

`test_every_corpus_fixture_grades_as_a_match` now walks all 48 fixtures in this repo, so the next narrowing cannot break the golden data silently. A throwaway probe confirmed the final form against all 192 fixtures across havel, foucault, and adorno.

## Tests

**299 tests, 1 failure.** That failure is `test_enforce_branch_name.BlockedCommandTest.test_match_carries_effective_git_context`, and it is environmental: the sandbox injects `credential.interactive` and two `url.insteadof` rewrites into git config, and the inherited test asserts an exact single-entry config list. It fails identically in all three sibling clones and passes in Actions. Inherited from `abuzucom/agents`, so it stands unmodified.

Every new assertion fails first against the unfixed code. `build_bundle.py --check`, `check_regime_refs.py`, and `run_eval.py` are unaffected and still clean.

## Scope

These are defects four and five in the family #1 fixed in `449d342`. All are present verbatim in `abuzucom/foucault` and `abuzucom/adorno`, and both ports are now open: abuzucom/foucault#7 and abuzucom/adorno#3.

CI proves no model behavior here. These assertions are structural.

pulls.body:
Bootstraps havel as the privacy-compliance member of the audit-prompt family, adapted from `abuzucom/foucault` and `abuzucom/adorno`.

This is one scaffold rather than a split change. The file list below separates inherited-verbatim, adapted, and new material so the diff stays reviewable.

## Design

Privacy rules are regime-conditional, so havel carries a second split axis neither sibling has.

- `AUDIT.md` is the hub at 27132 bytes against the 32768 ceiling. It holds regime-neutral practice, 29 class rows, and the workflow.
- `docs/checks/2.N.md` owns the mechanism: barrier list, severity posture, thresholds, investigation, boundaries.
- `docs/regimes/<slug>.md` owns the delta alone, referenced through the `[2.N@slug]` token.

A check file stating a statutory clock is a defect. A regime file explaining how to find a defect is a defect.

**Regime scope is declared, never inferred.** Applicability turns on facts absent from code: establishment, revenue, record volume, controller or processor role. The agent uses a declared scope, asks for one, or runs baseline classes alone and reports the scope as undeclared. Section 2A signals shape the question only; a signal-declaration mismatch raises no finding.

**Bundles are the delivery surface.** Pasting `AUDIT.md` alone would present 29 dead pointers. `scripts/build_bundle.py` generates 16 committed documents. Eight scopes ship a standard tier (32-49 KB) and a full tier (120-160 KB). Picking a bundle declares the scope, so the declared scope and the text the model holds cannot disagree.

## Divergences from the siblings

| Question | foucault | adorno | havel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blocking threshold | CRITICAL or HIGH | CRITICAL only | CRITICAL or HIGH |
| Blocker count | 9 | 5 | 10 |
| Concurrency rules | dropped | dropped | kept |
| `adopters/` | present | present | absent |

Two operating principles have no sibling equivalent: credit a control only after tracing it to effect, and classify by observed behavior rather than declared label. `docs/template-drift.md` records every divergence.

## Files

**Inherited verbatim from adorno** (26 files, hashes in `upstream-files.json`): all `scripts/*` checkers, `hooks/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.gitattributes`, and the upstream test helpers. `python scripts/check_upstream_drift.py --check-local` reports 26/26 matching.

**Adapted**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (adds regime-reference and bundle-currency steps), `.github/workflows/privacy-review.yml` (renamed, `ACCURACY` token, required `regimes` input, disclaimer grep), `eval/run_eval.py` (Data-map mode, scope validation, disclaimer check), `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `eval/README.md`, `docs/template-drift.md`.

**New**: `AUDIT.md`, 29 check files, 15 regime files plus `scope-profiles.md` and a generated matrix, `docs/scope-boundary.md`, `docs/legal-disclaimer.md`, `scripts/build_bundle.py`, `scripts/check_regime_refs.py`, `bundles.json`, 16 bundles, 103 eval cases, and five test modules.

## Verification

```
270 tests: 269 pass, 1 pre-existing environmental failure
build_bundle.py --check    OK
check_regime_refs.py       OK
run_eval.py                103 cases validated
check_upstream_drift.py    26/26 match
check_ascii, lint_style    clean (blocking)
```

Coverage policy sets the corpus size rather than a chosen number: one case per class, per blocker, per mode, per verdict-affecting regime delta, plus 15 negative controls. `undeclared-scope-file` is the load-bearing one, planting strong EU signals under an undeclared scope and asserting no GDPR finding appears.

## Known issues for review

**One test fails, and it is environmental.** `test_enforce_branch_name.BlockedCommandTest.test_match_carries_effective_git_context` fails identically in `abuzucom/adorno` on this machine. The sandbox injects `credential.interactive` and two `url.insteadof` rewrites into git config, and the inherited test asserts an exact single-entry config list. Rule 3 forbids editing an inherited test, so it stands unmodified.

**The hook allowlist blocks havel's own commands.** `hooks/enforce_branch_name.py` allowlists four upstream scripts. Every other invocation reads as an opaque command, so an agent session with hooks wired cannot run `check_regime_refs.py`, `build_bundle.py`, or `run_eval.py`. Human sessions and CI are unaffected. Adorno has the same gap with its own `run_eval.py`. The hook stays verbatim and `docs/template-drift.md` records the limitation; the fix belongs upstream in `abuzucom/agents`.

**CI proves no model behavior.** `run_eval.py` runs structure-only in CI because havel ships no credential and `--model-call` executes importable code. Every behavioral guarantee, including the negative controls and the disclaimer line, needs a live run. `docs/template-drift.md`, `eval/README.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` all state that split rather than implying CI covers it.

**Regime content needs a legal read.** Article and section references were written from knowledge of the regulations, not from a fetched read; the egress proxy blocks `eur-lex.europa.eu` and `gdpr.eu`. Every regime file carries `Last reviewed` and `Sources` for exactly this reason. Verify the thresholds and clocks before relying on them.

## Follow-ups outside this PR

- Port `build_bundle.py`, `bundles.json`, and the portable `test_bundles.py` assertions to foucault and adorno. Adorno needs it most: its `AUDIT.md` pasted alone points at 23 files the model cannot see.
- Open `adopters/havel.md` in `abuzucom/agents` per adoption step 18.
